A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DASH research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama training perplexities and optimizer timings, numerical convergence experiments, and additional Chebyshev experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds GPU-wide batching timings, damping comparisons, seed-level results and vision classification experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 extends existing layerwise batching to blocks across all layers assigned to one GPU. Appendix D adds a ViT adaptation that reshapes patch-embedding tensors into matrices. These refine the existing procedure; the inverse-root solvers and core Shampoo updates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates language modeling on C4. v2 retains this coverage and adds image classification on ImageNette and ImageWoof, substantially extending evaluation into a different data domain and task.

E2.justification: Table 4 newly evaluates SHMP, ABS-ADD and shifted-ReLU against one another; v1 only describes these damping approaches. The main Distributed Shampoo comparisons remain, and the vision experiments reuse the existing CN/NDB comparator families.

E3.justification: The existing Llama training budget, learning-rate search and block-size settings are retained. Added experiments introduce ViT-Tiny-5M and ViT-Small-21M with test accuracy, and damping comparisons at specified model sizes, block sizes and update frequencies. The vision training protocol is otherwise sparsely documented.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 adds an empirical test of whether the previously proposed damping heuristics improve perplexity. Table 1 also adds a direct comparison of layerwise and GPU-wide batching costs. Existing scaling, precision and Chebyshev analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 states that results average three seeds but omits standard deviations. v2 introduces seed identities, individual perplexities, means and standard deviations in Appendix C, plus uncertainty values in Table 5. Appendix C also discloses three-seed coverage for only a few experiments and lists two seeds for one configuration, contradicting the retained Section 5 statement. These reporting changes do not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the original results as layerwise timings and adds GPU-wide timings: for B=1024 and CN-FP16, 138 ms is retained and 119 ms is newly reported for the GPU variant. New damping, vision and seed-level outcomes substantially expand the evidence. Appendix C introduces unresolved discrepancies: B=1024 DASH-NDB Frobenius/PIM means are 11.692/11.726, versus 11.77/11.68 in Table 1.

T1.justification: The CN/NDB recurrences, matrix-scaling reasoning, Chebyshev derivations and damping mathematics are retained. The additions provide implementation adaptations and empirical evidence, without new proofs or revised theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens the maximum claimed optimizer-step speedup from 4.83x to 5.6x. The main contributions concerning block batching, inverse-root solvers and matrix scaling retain their original scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains the limited GPU-wide benefit for EVD, reports no clear winner among damping heuristics, and acknowledges insufficient compute for another damping setting. Appendix D explicitly limits architectural validation to Transformers and explains tensor reshaping through NDB's supported root exponents, while discussing the vision accuracy/runtime tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 distinguishes DASHGPU and DASHLAYERWISE implementations, documents ViT tensor reshaping and the exponents used when integrating NDB into Distributed Shampoo, and clarifies timing aggregation as a moving average over ten consecutive optimizer steps. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. Appendix D refers again to the original Shampoo work, rather than introducing a distinct citation or new novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 4.1 and Appendices C–D, expands local explanations and benchmarking prose to distinguish batching variants, and updates publication and acknowledgment text. The main narrative and existing appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the stacking diagram in Figure 3, expands Table 1 with separate layerwise/GPU timing columns, and adds damping, seed-statistics and vision tables. Table 3 receives header-formatting changes. These are localized display additions within the retained document layout.

improvement.justification: GPU-wide comparisons, the stacking diagram, and vision and damping experiments add useful evidence and clarity. However, Appendix C's means reverse the Frobenius/PIM ordering shown in Table 1, and its limited repeated-run coverage contradicts Section 5. These unresolved inconsistencies affect the central scaling conclusions and statistical credibility, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
